document_check.note: Wang Q, Yu R, Dong C, Zhou C, Xie Z, Sun H, Fu C, Zhu D. Association and prediction of Life's Essential 8 score, genetic susceptibility with MCI, dementia, and MRI indices: a prospective cohort study. J Affect Disord 2024;360:394-402. UK Biobank; 1797 (1.4%) incident MCI over a median 13.0 years; the limitation about health-conscious volunteers is present. Matches the review's Wang et al. 2024c.

cited_result: Cumulative incidence of ICD-10-coded MCI (G31.8, R41, F06.7) in UK Biobank: 1797 of 126,785 cognitively unimpaired participants (1.4%) over a median 13.0 years of hospital-inpatient and death-record linkage. The review also cites the authors' stated limitation that health-conscious volunteers may have led to underestimated incidence.
tool_reason: The cited result is an incidence proportion (the share of participants who accrued a coded MCI diagnosis), so the JBI checklist for prevalence and incidence studies applies. The paper's hazard ratios and AUCs are not the cited result.

domains.domain: 1. Sample frame appropriate to the target population
domains.rationale: This is a volunteer cohort aged 40-69 that the authors state is more health-conscious than the general population, and they note this may lower incidence.

signalling.question: Was the sample frame appropriate to address the target population?
signalling.quote: participants who volunteered in the UK Biobank were more health-conscious than the general population (Batty et al., 2020), which may have underestimated the incidence of MCI and dementia.

domains.rationale: The analysis is restricted to the 139,257 participants with complete LE8 data (roughly a quarter of the more than 500,000 cohort), minus those with missing covariates. It is a complete-case subset with no comparison of included and excluded participants.

signalling.question: Were study participants sampled in an appropriate way?
signalling.quote: Among 139,257 participants who had completed data on LE8 components, a total of 126,785 participants (including an imaging subsample of 25,312 participants) were included in the analysis after excluding 12,472 participants who were already diagnosed MCI or all-cause dementia at baseline (n = 221) and those with missing data on potential covariates (n = 12,251)

domains.rationale: With 126,785 participants, precision is not a concern.

signalling.question: Was the sample size adequate?
signalling.quote: We included 126,785 participants with a mean (SD) age of 56.0 (8.0) years and 53.5 % were female.

domains.rationale: The assessment centres, age range and baseline characteristics by outcome (Table 1) are reported.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: Participants attended 1 of 22 assessment centers across England, Wales, and Scotland, where they completed the touchscreen questionnaire, underwent physiological measurement, and provided biological samples at a baseline assessment visit.

domains.rationale: Outcomes were ascertained by record linkage for every included participant, so there is no differential loss to follow-up in the analysed sample.

signalling.question: Was the data analysis conducted with sufficient coverage of the identified sample?
signalling.quote: Participants gave informed consent for data linkage to national hospital inpatient admissions

domains.domain: 6. Valid methods for identification of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI was defined by three ICD-10 codes, including the symptom code R41 and G31.8, found in hospital inpatient and death records. No validation of these codes for MCI is reported; the high-positive-predictive-value statement belongs to the UK Biobank dementia algorithm. MCI diagnosed outside hospital admissions would be missed.

signalling.question: Were valid methods used for the identification of the condition?
signalling.quote: The International Classification of Diseases (ICD) coding system was used to define MCI (ICD-10 codes: G31.8, R41, and F06.7). All-cause dementia (Field 42018) ... The algorithm was developed by the UK Biobank outcome adjudication group to classify disease outcomes with high positive predictive value.

domains.domain: 7. Condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all
domains.rationale: The same linked-record ascertainment and censoring date applied to every participant.

signalling.question: Was the condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Hospital inpatient data and death data were censored on 30 November 2022

domains.rationale: Incidence is given only as a crude proportion, with no confidence interval, no person-time rate and no account of competing death. The numerator is internally inconsistent: Table 1's 'developed MCI' column sums to 1425 (592 + 833; 1.1%), against 1797 in the text and in Table 2.

signalling.question: Was there appropriate statistical analysis?
signalling.quote: After a median of 13.0 years of follow-up, 1797 (1.4 %) cognitively unimpaired people developed MCI

signalling.question: Are numerator and denominator reported consistently?

domains.rationale: The UK Biobank recruitment response rate is not reported. The healthy-volunteer effect is acknowledged but not handled, for example by weighting.

signalling.question: Was the response rate adequate, and if not, was the low response rate managed appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for response rate, number invited, participation proportion and weighting. None is reported beyond the acknowledgement of health-conscious volunteers (p. 8).

overall: High (JBI prevalence under this review's rule: 'valid methods for identification of the condition' (item 6) and 'appropriate statistical analysis' (item 8) are both No).
overall_rationale: The incidence estimate rests on unvalidated, broad ICD codes in hospital inpatient and death records. It comes from a health-conscious volunteer complete-case subset, is reported without a confidence interval or person-time rate, and has an internally inconsistent numerator. Any of items 6 or 8 at No makes the rating high.

applicability.rationale: This is a predominantly White, health-conscious volunteer cohort aged 40-69 at baseline, with hospital-record ascertainment only. The 1.4% describes coded ascertainment in this cohort, not population MCI incidence. The review's wording, scoped to 'registry-linked ICD-coded ascertainment in UK Biobank', respects this.
